header.running_head: The Practices of Nabi ﷺ and the Sahabah (RA) with Regard to Clothing

blocks.text: The Practices of Hadhrat Ali (RA) With Regard to Clothing

Hadhrat Zaid bin Wahab narrates that a delegation from Basrah once came to see Hadhrat Ali (RA). Amongst them was a man belonging to the Khawaarij whose name was Ja'd bin Na'ja. When he started criticising Hadhrat Ali (RA)'s clothing, Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "What problem have you got with my clothing when it is far away from pride and a most appropriate example for the people to follow." [^2]
Hadhrat Amr bin Qais reports that when someone asked Hadhrat Ali (RA) why he patched his Qamees, he replied, "The heart humbles with it and the Mu'min is able to follow the example." [^3]
Hadhrat Ataa Abu Muhammad says, "I once saw Hadhrat Ali (RA) wearing an unwashed Qamees made of extremely coarse cloth." [^4]

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abu Hudhayl reports, "I once saw on Hadhrat Ali bin Abi Taalib (RA) a Qamees made in Ray which was such that when he stretched out his arms, the sleeves reached the ends of his fingers and when he retracted them, they reached close to halfway up his forearms." [^5]

Whenever Hadhrat Ali (RA) wore a Qamees, he would pull the sleeve until it reached his fingers. He would then cut off what was extra (extending further than the fingers) saying, "The sleeves should never extend further than the hands." [^6]

Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Azdi who was one of the Imaams of the Azd tribe reports that he once saw Hadhrat Ali (RA) come to the marketplace and say, "Who has a good Qamees for three Dirhams?" When one of the traders said that he had one, Hadhrat Ali (RA) went to him and liked the Qamees very much. "This must be worth more (than three Dirhams)!" Hadhrat Ali (RA) remarked (thinking that the man was reducing the price because Hadhrat Ali (RA) was the Ameerul Mu'mineen). "Not at all," the man replied, "that is really the price." Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed says that he then saw Hadhrat Ali (RA) untie a knot in his clothing containing some Dirhams and giving it to the trader. Hadhrat Ali (RA) then wore the Qamees, which happened extend past the ends of his fingers. By his instruction, the excess that extended past his fingers was then cut off. [^7]
